newsitem.title: CANADA: TrizecHahn closes deal to lease CN Tower.
newsitem.headline: TrizecHahn closes deal to lease CN Tower.

text.p: TrizecHahn Corp on Thursday said it closed its agreement with the Canadian government to lease Toronto's landmark CN Tower.
The Toronto-based real estate company said the transaction is valued at C$108 million, including C$46 million paid at the closing and the present value of future lease payments.

TrizecHahn also said it intends to begin a C$20 million renovation of the tower this October. The renovations include adding interactive entertainment, improving the food and retail outlets at the base, streamlining entrances and redesigning the base's interior.

Under the final agreement, TrizecHahn will lease the CN Tower for an initial 40-year period with two 15-year renewal options. The company has also acquired 151 Front Street, a 250,000-square-foot mixed-use building and SkyWalk, an enclosed pedestrian walkway linking Toronto's Union Station and the CN Tower.
When negotiations on the agreement were made public in March, TrizecHahn said it would operate the tower for an initial 35 years with two 15-year renewal options.

TrizecHahn President Gregory Wilkins said in a statement that the tower represented an outstanding opportunity and the company planned to capitalize on the six million tourists who visited the area each year.
TrizecHahn shares fell 0.20 to 30.40 in late afternoon trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange. The company's shares closed at an all-time high in Toronto of 33.30 on February 11.
